Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-permanence-finite-type: local finite type is preserved under composition

Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-type-surjective-geometric-points: a nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field has a k-valued point
core_obligations: Since U and R are locally of finite type over B, the morphisms s, t, j and phi are locally of finite type by the permanence lemma; the geometric-point lemma will be used without further mention

Assume phi is an orbit space; fix an algebraically closed field k over B and a point x-bar of X(k); the fibre product of U over phi with Spec of k at x-bar is a nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over k, hence has a k-valued point, which proves the displayed map is surjective

If u-bar and u-bar-prime in U(k) map to the same point of X(k), the orbit definition makes them lie in the same R-orbit, and the geometric-orbits lemma upgrades this to equivalence under the relation generated by j(R(k)); hence the displayed map is injective

Conversely assume the displayed map is bijective for every algebraically closed k over B; bijectivity gives surjectivity of phi, R-invariance holds by assumption, and the injectivity of the displayed maps says precisely that phi separates orbits; hence phi is an orbit space
proof_roadmap: Prove surjectivity and injectivity of the orbit map on k-valued points from the orbit space axioms using the nonempty fibre product argument
Conversely read bijectivity of the orbit maps as surjectivity, invariance, and orbit separation
